subject.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins

question: Should the plugin-update area land this broader branch, land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107063 and track the update-check parser separately, or retain the current fail-closed policy?
rationale: Both branches are proof-positive and overlap the same state-mutation boundary, while this branch additionally changes a sibling parser; automation cannot safely choose the canonical branch or approve the broader failure-policy contract.

options.title: Land this broader branch
options.body: Refresh this PR against current main, rerun exact-head checks, and use it as the single canonical fix for both state preservation and singleton-array update metadata.

options.title: Land the narrower competitor
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107063 for state preservation and open a separate focused change for the update-check parser normalization.

options.title: Retain fail-closed behavior
options.body: Pause both PRs if owners conclude that non-E404 metadata failures must continue disabling installed plugins despite the demonstrated configuration-loss impact.

recommendation.title: Land this broader branch
recommendation.body: Refresh this PR against current main, rerun exact-head checks, and use it as the single canonical fix for both state preservation and singleton-array update metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant update lifecycle and parser behavior trace directly to this person's prior commits, making them the strongest available owner for selecting the permanent failure policy.
